summary: Separate local implementation, code shipping and explicitly approved multi-PR release publication, with exact generated release-document verification.
userImpact: Merged code changes can accumulate in one pending release instead of automatically publishing a release after the first PR.

instructions: Set RELEASE_AUTOPILOT_ENABLED=false, reinstall the maintained workflow plugin, and use /release to publish the complete agreed batch through the explicit source/tag/PR dispatch.

configuration: Release Please push and schedule runs prepare release PRs without tagging. Publication dispatch requires publish_release=true, source_ref, release_tag, release_pr and required_prs.
The workflow plugin advances independently to 0.1.15; /new-change stops locally and /ship excludes Release Please PRs.
Legacy release-autopilot and hotfix auto-merge inputs are retained but cannot authorize a release.
Release-control CI includes a five-minute read-only authorization canary, required by ci-complete; it creates no public tags, packages or images.

notes: No application schema or historical migration change.

security: Automatic events, labels and autopilot settings cannot authorize production tag creation. Publication requires an exact protected source, merged batch ancestry, generated document and managed-comment equality, and the existing signed candidate proof.
documentation: Technical release-process and plugin documentation define command authority, batch composition, documentation generation and the explicit publication inputs. Legacy workflow entrypoints delegate to the maintained skills.
knownLimitations: The release merge/publication interval is frozen; a change to protected main invalidates the approved source and stops publication.
rollback: Restore the prior workflow only through an explicitly authorized change; do not alter published tags or bypass candidate validation.
validation: Node 24.10.0: 144 targeted release/workflow/classifier tests passed, including 34 behavioral cases using the actual GitHub-script bodies and temporary real Git repositories. Automatic events created no release tags; incomplete batches, live-main drift and inconsistent generated documents were rejected.

The complete CI contract suite passed 178 tests and its aggregate coverage guard; all 92 change-detection/security contracts and 65 release-note tests passed. Warning-free workspace lint, release-note preflight, documentation-boundary and published-package version guards passed. Actionlint workflow validation passed; full CI ShellCheck reports six unchanged baseline diagnostics outside the added job.

All 11 workflow-plugin contracts and official validation of all 25 skills passed. The supplemental Python plugin-manifest validator is absent locally; the official bundled Codex installer accepted plugin 0.1.15, and installed skill bytes match the maintained source.
The actual previous #563 merge-group commit contains its PR head, confirming the new per-PR ancestry guard applies to the recorded failure.

The focused canary passed nine local scenarios using the actual approval CLI and production signed-candidate shell step: automatic events, incomplete approval, source drift and mismatched documentation fail closed; a complete fixture approval reaches the real verifier, which rejects its missing staged candidate. Disposable Git/API fixtures carry no production authority or tokens. The exact-source hosted canary remains required before merge and does not replace signed production candidate, image, database, browser or security acceptance.

Live RELEASE_AUTOPILOT_ENABLED is false. No production publication, semantic tag, registry write or deployment was performed; source-level qualification and protected hosted acceptance remain distinct.
